CONF1.question: A cube of plastic scintillator 31 cm on a side (30 L) is surrounded by 5 cm of polyethylene, and about 540 inverse beta decays per day occur in it. Ambient radioactivity produces single energy deposits above 1 MeV at 80 Hz per square metre of its outer surface, mostly from the 1.46 and 2.61 MeV gamma lines. Positrons must be accepted from 1 MeV upward. If the neutrons are tagged by capture on gadolinium (an approximately 8 MeV gamma cascade), with any choice of delayed energy threshold, coincidence window and hit-multiplicity cut, can the delayed capture signal be recorded for at least 30% of the inverse beta decays while the accidental prompt-delayed coincidence rate stays below the detected signal rate? End your answer with one line: VERDICT: YES or VERDICT: NO.
